notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0003] Reject bools when validating integer fields: When validating an int field such as quantity, check isinstance(x, bool) first because bool is a subclass of int; use `isinstance(quantity, bool) or not isinstance(quantity, int) or quantity <= 0`.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Round money only via round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Validation failures raise BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors with codes like "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity", "negative_amount"; reuse the existing code names rather than inventing new ones, and include the offending value in the detail string.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

item.title: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc
item.content: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).

candidate.title: Raise BillingError with a code string
candidate.content: Signal invalid billing inputs by raising `BillingError` from `ledgerly.errors` with a short snake_case code plus a detail argument, e.g. `BillingError("before_start", at.isoformat())`.

candidate.content: Subscription periods are `timedelta(days=sub.period_days)` blocks counted from `sub.started_at`; compute the block index with floor division `(at - start) // length` as `current_period` does.
